draft.title: Homeostasis
card: Homeostasis is the process of keeping the internal environment of the body stable, within a narrow range, even when the outside conditions change. Body temperature, blood glucose and water balance are examples.
A stimulus is a change in the internal or external environment. A receptor is a cell or structure that detects the stimulus.
The control centre receives information from the receptor and decides what to do. In humans it is often the brain, such as the hypothalamus.
An effector, such as a muscle or gland, carries out the instruction. The change it produces is the response.
draft.remember: Homeostasis works as a chain: stimulus, receptor, control centre, effector, response.

a.q: On a hot day, skin cells detect that the body is warming up. Which part of the pathway are these skin cells?
a.why: The skin cells detect the change, so they are receptors. Effectors are the parts that carry out the instruction, such as sweat glands, and they act after the control centre has processed the information.

b.q: Sam walks into a cold room. His brain receives signals about the cold and sends instructions to his muscles, which start to shiver. Which part of the pathway is the brain in this case?
b.why: The brain receives information and sends instructions, so it is the control centre. The muscles are the effector because they carry out the instruction, and the cold is the stimulus.
b.clue: Which part receives information and decides what to do?

problems.detail: The stem says the skin cells 'detect' the change, which is the exact word the card uses to define a receptor. A student can match the keyword without understanding the pathway.

The stem says the brain 'receives signals' and 'sends instructions', which closely mirrors the card's definition of the control centre. The answer can be found by matching words rather than applying the idea.

proposal.title: Homeostasis
card: Homeostasis is the process of keeping the internal environment of the body stable, within a narrow range, even when the outside conditions change. Body temperature, blood glucose and water balance are examples.
A stimulus is a change in the internal or external environment. A receptor is a cell or structure that detects the stimulus.
The control centre receives information from the receptor and decides what to do. In humans it is often the brain, such as the hypothalamus.
An effector, such as a muscle or gland, carries out the instruction. The change it produces is the response.
proposal.remember: Homeostasis works as a chain: stimulus, receptor, control centre, effector, response.

a.q: A house has a thermostat that switches on a heater when the room gets cold. If this worked like homeostasis, what part would the heater play?
a.why: The heater is the part that carries out the instruction and changes the room's temperature, so it acts as the effector. The thermostat is the tempting choice for the receptor or control centre, but it is the part that senses the cold and switches the heater on, not the part that warms the room.
a.clue: Which part actually makes the change happen?

b.q: During a run, carbon dioxide builds up in Ella's blood. Sensors in her blood vessels signal her brainstem, then her diaphragm works harder. Which part of the pathway is her faster breathing?
b.why: Faster breathing is the change that results, so it is the response. The diaphragm is the effector, because it is the muscle that does the work. The rise in carbon dioxide is the stimulus, and the brainstem is the control centre.
b.clue: Is faster breathing a body part, or a change that happens?
